INTRODUCTION
In this day and age of cut throat competition, it becomes all
the more important for people to utilize their full mental
capacity in order to achieve the heights of success. Not doing
so might result in being left behind, while the competition
forges ahead.
All human beings have the potential to multitask and can
finish arduous tasks within a matter of minutes. But not
everybody is able to do so, and only those that truly
capitalizes on their mental abilities, by training their minds
to delve into the depths of knowledge, will be able to attain
due success!
There will always be winners and those that will look up to
them in envy. If everybody were to be the former, then we
would end up in a world where no competition would exist.
However, the main goal for most humans is to be a winner
and leave the competition behind.
So what is it that helps these winners achieve the kind of
success that they experience in life and what do the others
lack? Well, the answer lies in three simple letters, NLP.
NLP stands for Neuro Linguistic Programming and refers to
concept that allows people to control their own and other
people’s minds, while influencing thought and behavior; to
attain more out of life.
In this book, we will look at the meaning of NLP, explore its
core concepts and also see how you can implement it in your
day-to-day life. There are specific chapters dedicated to
understanding the concept of NLP, exploring its meaning,
steps to implement in your life and also a few tips on small
talk.
I thank you for choosing this book and hope you have a good
time reading it.
Let us begin.
CHAPTER 1
WHAT IS NLP?
NLP is a core concept of psychology. It stands for Neuro
Linguistic Programming.
NLP was first introduced in 1970 by Richard Brandler and
John Grinder. Grinder, a linguistics expert and Brandler an
author, explored the dimensions of human psychology in
terms of mind and behavior control.
They were some of the first ones to tell humans that it is
possible to attain more from life by making use of both sides
of the brain. They are said to have been heavily influenced
by the work of psychologists Virginia Satir, Milton
Erickson and Fritz Perls.
In fact, Brandler closely worked with Perls and Satir to come
up with the different ideologies of NLP.
NLP mainly deals with people capitalizing on their
brainpower and doing more by tapping into their complete
mental capacity.
I know it sounds a bit complex but it is actually quite easy.
You have to first understand the basic concept and then go
about exploiting it. Through the course of this book, we will
look at how you can do so with ease.
Through extensive study or educated people, Brandler and
Grinder found that despite having similar educational
backgrounds, some people were able to exploit their
education and do more in their life whereas some were
unable to put it to good use and would end up failing at
finishing the task at hand.
This made them realize that having good education alone
was not helping these people succeed and there was
something more that was allowing them to forge ahead. They
decided to investigate and find out what really set these
successful people apart and what extra they possessed that
helped them get to where they were.
Once they were done with their research, they were surprised
to know that the successful people had a different way of
communicating with others, which helped them succeed
better. The ones that were not succeeding as much were not
able to communicate with others well enough. So, they
decided to compile a set of rules that would allow people to
communicate better and thus the concepts of NLP were
formed.
What sets NLP apart from the rest of the concepts that are
out there is the fact that it mainly deals with focusing on the
solution as opposed to the problem. Many psychologists
spend a lot of time listening to a person’s problems and make
a big deal out of trying to analyze and present these
problems. However, NLP will focus on the solution and
come up with a feasible one that help the person implement
it with ease.
NLP is a concept where people make use of the information
that they have and try to apply it practically in the different
real life situations that they come across on a daily basis. As
you know, everybody is required to take full advantage of
their education and that can be done through the
implementation of NLP. Communication is a key aspect and
NLP teaches people to both communicate internally with
themselves and also externally with the outside world.
The concept is generally taught by experts who have
extensive knowledge on the subject. Many schools and
colleges now make use of NLP to teach students and help
them understand how they can use their existing knowledge
and put it to good use.
Problem solving is one of the main implementations of NLP.
It is not limited to looking at the issue through a single
viewpoint and deals with analyzing it through several
different viewpoints before arriving at a feasible solution. It
is about expanding the horizons of thought and looking at
the bigger picture.
Now you might be wondering as to who is NLP for? And
whether you will be able to take it up and implement it in
your life.
NLP will be beneficial for a whole host of people and there
is no hard and fast rule that says only certain types of people
can take it up. Let us look at who can truly benefit by
employing the theories of NLP in their life.
Working professionals will have the chance to maximize
their career opportunities by making use of NLP. As you
know, everybody in the rat race wishes to outdo the other in
order to be a leader. With the help of NLP, the person will
know to make a quick decision and find a solution that will
help solve a problem. He or she will also be able to deal with
everyday issues with ease thereby increasing their level of
productivity.
Students can make use of NLP to excel in their studies. NLP
mainly deals with enhancing internal communication and the
child will be able to remember the concepts better, and for a
longer period of time. NLP is a simple concept and children
will not have to take up rigorous mental tasks to understand
and implement it. Parents can start introducing the concept
to them and they will successfully get their child started on
it.
NLP is also for elders. It will help in making their everyday
life easy. They will not have to put in too much effort to find
solutions to their problems and they can extrapolate and
arrive at quick and feasible solutions to their issues. NLP is a
technique that many elders employ in their day-to-day life,
as it is quite simple to understand as well.
Remember that the different problems that you will come
across will all have the same thing at their core and you will
have to get to it and make use of your common knowledge to
solve them.
MIND CONTROL AND COERCION
Mind control and coercion are two different things. Mind
control isn’t coercion and it doesn’t make use of any of the
tricks or techniques that are made use of in coercion.
Coercion is the act where the controller wants to have his
own way, regardless of the feelings, emotions or thoughts of
the person whom he is coercing. Threats, humiliation and
even guilt can be made use of for achieving the end result in
coercion. By now you would have understood that there isn’t
anything positive about coercion. To coerce an individual
means that you are forcefully making them behave or act in a
certain manner that they didn’t want to and this isn’t what
mind control is about. In mind control you don’t force an
individual to go against their basic beliefs.
The stark difference between coercion and mind control is
that coercion doesn’t understand the workings of the mind of
the person who is being coerced. Coercion is used by most
of the cults and leaders for controlling the minds of others. If
you have read the Harry Potter books or have seen the
movies then you would realize that Lord Voldemort made
use of coercion for controlling people by threatening to kill
or torture them if they don’t follow him.
MIND CONTROL AND PERSUASION
Mind control and persuasion are closely interlinked.
However, they are different from one another. It is important
that you understand the difference between these two. For
getting a better idea of this concept, take into consideration
Maslow’s theory. Every human being has certain needs and
these needs can be noted down in the form of a pyramid
according to the order of achieving self-actualization.
Persuasion would rest at the bottom of such a pyramid, along
with all the other basic needs. On the other hand, mind
control would be at the top of the pyramid along with self-
actualization. Persuasion forms the basis for obtaining
control over the mind.
As you keep progressing through higher levels, more control
and power would be exercised on the mind and when this
power has reached its maximum, and then you will be able
to control your mind. A simple example would help you get
a better understanding of this concept. For instance, you
want the latest MacBook, but you need your parent’s or your
spouse’s permission for buying it. But when you make use of
mind control, you will be able to tell yourself that you
cannot do without that gadget and you will figure out a way
in which you can acquire it by making it seem acceptable to
others.
You will need to remember that it is very difficult to control
a person’s mind and you will need to think beyond the
present situation at hand, if you want to really control a
person’s mind. Most of us function with the belief that if we
react to a situation in a certain manner, it will help us achieve
the outcome that we desire. Therefore, it is safe to say that
mind control is all about strategic thinking.
You will need to think ahead, if you want to achieve the
outcome you truly desire. This in itself is not an easy task,
you will need to understand the manner in which a person
thinks and also identify the responses that such an individual
would give to specific situations. But for doing all this, you
will need to have a thorough understanding of yourself. You
should be able to control your emotions; impulses and you
must be secretive about your goals because this is the fastest
manner in which you will be able to reach them. In the next
chapter you will find the different ways in which a person
thinks and this will help you understand them better.
WHERE IS MIND CONTROL USED?
Mind control is a process that is used on a daily basis and
this section will give you a few examples of mind control
that you would encounter in your daily life. The manner in
which you motive your child or other students at school to
perform better, instilling the belief of God in yourself and
your children requires a certain degree of mind control,
instill a sense of superiority in a particular group like the
classic distinction between the jocks and the nerds, attracting
a person into a relationship whether it is a professional or a
personal relationship, teaching your swim team to display
contempt against their competitors, convincing a person to
buy a particular product, convincing a policeman to let go of
you without getting a ticket for violating any traffic laws and
convincing others to give up on their belief and follow your
beliefs. I could keep going on and on.
The person, who is making use of mind control, clearly
knows his goals. It is true that when you want something
truly, then you will motivate the concerned person to finish
the task for you. This is a form of mind control technique
that’s made use of in everyday life. There are simple
examples of mind control all around you. For instance, a
child would clean their room because their parents have
conditioned them since a very young age that it is better to
have a clean room. This is a subtle form of mind control.
Mind control is used everywhere and you will need to learn
to either accept it or learn how to make use of it yourself.
Obviously it would be a better option to learn it so that you
can use it for your own advantage. Mind control is about
influencing a person’s mindset so that it would be beneficial
for you and for doing this you will need to put in some
effort. During the time of elections, we see a lot of people
who are trying to do this. The political leaders, in a bid to get
your votes, they give speeches that address various issues
and this is actually a method of mind control. The speeches
that they give are designed and written in such a way that
they would get them the maximum possible votes. The party
knows that in areas where the number of votes they are
going to get is low, then in such areas the speeches are
written so that they could motivate and encourage people to
vote for them. The advertisements on television also make
use of the same technique. The advertisements that we see
will leave an impression on our subconscious mind and
that’s why we tend to retain what we see. For instance, if an
advert says that cutting down on salt would be good for
health, chances are that we will not only start practicing that
unconsciously but we will also pass on the same message to
others as well.
The main problem with mind control is that it is not just
about positive things; it can even lead you to believe things
that aren’t as simple as we thought they were when portrayed
in the advertisements. For instance, all the cosmetic
companies keep coming up with new ingredients that they
keep adding to their products that pretty much baffle the
audience. If you watch an advertisement for a cosmetic
product the next time, you will notice that the advertisers
design the advertisement in such a way that it gives the
impression to the viewers as if they are learning something
new and the viewers will definitely remember what they
“learned” from the advert and end up buying the product.
The point here is that, subliminal messages are capable of
changing people’s mindset in a very subtle way.
Mind control is about understanding the mindset of others
and adjusting the tasks in such a manner that it would give a
positive feedback. Follow this book to learn more about
mind control.
CHAPTER 2
HOW PEOPLE THINK
People can generally be categorized into three broad
categories based on the manner of their thinking and these
are as follows.
SERIAL THINKING
Humans are all programmed to react in different manner to
different situations. The intensity of the reaction varies from
one person to another and this reaction is without any
conscious thought. This method ensures that we don't think
about it. This kind of thinking has been associated to
lemmings walking over a cliff top. Serial thinkers are the
ones who will follow the masses regardless of whether the
direction the masses are headed in was safe or not.
LINEAR THINKING
Linear thinking is very different from serial thinking. In
serial thinking there is no conscious thought process that
takes place, whereas in linear thinking there's a lot of thought
that goes into it. It not only involves the ability to understand
and predict the probable outcomes of the actions you do, but
it also makes you think about the most efficient course of
action that can be adopted for meeting the goal. For getting a
better understanding of this concept, think of it as a game of
chess where you not only have to think about the move you
are making but also analyze the move to understand the
likely moves your opponent could make. So, it is about
analyzing a situation, thinking about the pros and cons of
each situation and predicting the likely outcome in a logical
manner. Linear thinking is easy to deal with when you are
working on mind control because you are able to anticipate
that the subject matter will have to go through a detailed
analysis of the minute details that would eventually lead to
the desired conclusion. If you can manage to tap into these
thoughts, you will definitely be able to change them to play
in your favor.
NON – LINEAR THINKING
Non-linear thinking is a step above linear thinking. It can
even incorporate the dimensions of time and space. If you
have watched the movie Sherlock Holmes in the movie
Game of Shadows, this is a classic example of non-linear
thinking. He analyses every move that he wants to make and
at the same time also analyses the ways in which he can play
the game better while understanding the moves that would
be beneficial for him. At the end of the movie he even
manages to stages his own death so that he can catch the bag
guys red-handed. He portrays what a non-linear thinking
man would be like. These thinkers, they think outside the
box but their intuition always guides them. They notice
things that are seldom noticed by others and this makes their
point of view much different from the rest. Such individuals
will prove to be difficult subjects to exercise mind control
over but it is possible if you can mange to understand their
mindset and lay traps that would lead them to the conclusion
that you want them to reach. There was a non-linear thinker
in the character Patrick Jane from a popular TV series, The
Mentalist, he was capable of reading people and often
noticed things that others didn't see. This ability is there
within every single one of us, but not many make use of it
and that is the only difference between non-linear thinkers
and the rest.
ETHICS OF MIND CONTROL
Like every other discipline, even this area of study has
certain ethics that need to be followed while practicing it. Of
course, these ethics aren't hard and fast rules. There are
numerous people all over the world who have made use of
mind control techniques for achieving their goals and
dreams. Some people are extremely good at this and can
make other individuals feel that what they are doing is
beneficial for them. Then there are some who haven't got any
skills in this regard and their actions can have dire
consequences. Therefore, it's advisable that you make use of
these practices on people whom you are comfortable with. If
you don't find the practices of mind control an annoyance
when they are used on you, then you can go ahead a day use
them on others. There's another thing that you should keep in
your mind and it's that you shouldn't make use of money
control when you are angry, hurt or are extremely emotional,
because you wouldn't be in a situation to understand or
worry about the consequences of your actions on others.
Emotions tend to get in the way of logic and your actions
could hurt those on whom you were performing mind
control. However, you need to be mindful of the fact that
those people could hurt you in a manner similar to the one
that you tried hurting them in. Negative thoughts are copse
of altering the thought process and the individual wouldn't
be able to think in a coherent manner that's consistent with
linear thinking. Those who make use of mind control in a
negative manner are those individuals who seek to have
power over someone else. The mentally abided housewife
would put up with her husband and control her because she
is in a very fragile psychological state. The abuser would
make use of this to further weaken his partner. This is an
example of improper use of mind control.
You might want to inform your friends about the knowledge
that you possess on mind control. My sincere request would
be that you refrain from doing that. You wouldn’t want your
dear ones to start thinking that any change in their behavior
is due to your influence on them. Instead it would be better
to let them realize all this on their own without your
interference. There is another thing that you should do; you
need to ask yourself why it is important to read someone’s
mind for you. If your answer is that you want to obtain a
greater understanding of how the human mind reasons, then
you have got a very good reason and sufficient motive to go
ahead with it. But, if you are making use of mind control for
any negative reasons, then you shouldn’t use mind control
because it would amount to coercion if you want to force
someone to do or abstain from doing an act that isn’t in sync
with their well being and is against their will. Human beings
are blessed with intelligence so that they could help in
making things better for themselves and those who are
around them and its intention isn’t to make someone else’s
life worse. Therefore, when you are using mind control,
please make sure that you are doing it for the right reasons.
TYPES OF PEOPLE
You will need to remember that there are two types of people
when it comes to using mind control. There are some people
who are controlled by their emotions and then there are

Most of the time, my grandfather’s pub was crowded, and they
recommended a bottle, and soon after, my parents had a successful business
with all the local businesses coming for lunch.
When I was a teenager, I helped in a bar. One minute I was discussing
how I wanted to become a CPA with President Rothmans, and the next
moment I was serving a village idiot on a public tape listening to the jokes
he had made.
“Nick,” said Jack. “What happens if a nail falls into the Red Sea?”
“Wait a minute, Jack. I just need to serve President Rothmans’ gin and
tonic. I’ll be back with you for a minute Jack, what was that joke? Oh yes, I
remember something on the nail, I’m sorry, I don’t know.
“Nothing,” was his response.
“Nothing?”
“Yes. Nothing. Because you would lose it.”
Jack never joked well; I bet you’ve never heard that before.
My point here is that I had to continually adapt and change my
personality to suit the person I was serving. I didn’t understand it then, but
at a young age, I acquired valuable equalizer skills.
We were also lucky with large local businesses, and on Friday evening,
we had lawyers, accountants, salespeople, engineers, and a few independent
billionaires. So when I was ready to start my business career, I felt like I
had met most types of people, which meant I could adapt. The only problem
is that I decided to become a CPA and that required a “certain” personality.
No.
Anyway, I started my CPA training, and I remember a day when I was
working in an audit room. Another articulated employee had just joined
and, like me, was probably doing the wrong job. We got along well, and we
talked while we were working. At that moment, the head of the audit
entered and separated us, without speaking! My new colleague had to go to
the library to work. I never knew how I spent five and a half years in this
business.
At that time, I was playing my best golf. I managed to win two club
championships in a row, which allowed me to dream, hoping that one day I
could turn to a professional and leave the world of debit and credit. But my
escape from auditing and accounting was close I just needed to discover
another world. A world where having a personality was very important.
So if you don’t have an excellent natural equivalent (EQ) or if you
haven’t been fortunate enough to have been raised in a pub, what can you
do to become an excellent sales representative?
Well, the second-best option is to learn to deal with people. When I
was working as a UK sales manager for JD Edwards, the vice president of
our region at the time convinced me to take a sales course called “Sales
Empathy”. I was in my thirties, and it’s one thing at this age to think that
you know everything; no, you don’t think you know you do everything!
Since I retired from the business to run my video and marketing
business, I had read more business books than when I was younger, books
that would make me even better. You never stop learning, and anyone who
bought this book and made it to the end should hopefully look for a few tips
and tricks you didn’t know before and become a better seller. Boys will stop
learning and adopt information that will continue to be wrong; there are 10
to 13 disabled players who never reach a single number because they reject
a lesson or two.
In the same way that it is always good to see your golf professional
from time to time because errors can enter your game; it is a good idea to
buy books for sale or to go on new land.
Anyway, we started the “Sales Empathy” training, and it was just
amazing, it was like the light was on. It was the answer to the question of
why I can communicate better than other providers. Over the years, I have
unconsciously trained in the pub on how to respond to different personality
styles.
Empathy has been to provide a framework for personality - a structure
that divided people into seven fundamental emotions.
1. Hustler: the desire for money.
2. Standard: the desire for social approval.
3. Driver: Desire to communicate.
4. Double-check: the desire for security.
5. Artist: The passion for creativity.
6. Politics: the desire to win.
7. Engineer: Desire to carry out projects.
Most people now have two or three dominant emotions, as well as one
for balance (normal).
You can determine what kind of person they are by simply looking at
their behavior, how they dress, the car they drive, their position in the
business, office hours, how they speak, and whether they are waiting for a
meeting.
I used this framework extensively in JD Edwards, then in GL, where
we added all of these fields to the CRM system so that when you look at the
account, you can quickly see what kind of perspective you have.
Selling empathy is a missing link and, in my opinion, it should be
included in every book written in EQ because it explains HOW to discover
your underlying emotions and the emotions of others.
Sell personalities as much as one person.
People “like” people who look like them. Adapt your approach to your
audience:
If you sell to an engineer, give them details.
Artists need technical features and design - ask them to imagine the
benefits of dreaming.
Beginners want an overview, and they want it quickly.
Politicians don’t want to back down, so you have to sell them slowly
and influence them indirectly to come up with an idea.
Double control is secure; they must be careful not to lose the business
if they buy it.
Normal people want references.
Search engines want discounts and names of prestigious companies
that use your product or service.
If you are a manager, Sales Empathy can also be used to help recruit
sales representatives.
By the way, the best point of sale profiles is the highest points for
Hustlers, Movers, and Politika. We get occasional engineers who can be
sold, but they will need high movement scores and politicians in their
dominant traits.
Combining Miller Heiman with commercial empathy
What’s interesting is when you combine the above personality types
with the Miller Heiman customer types. For example, IT staff will typically
be made up of two engineers/testers; Details and rapports are required for
decision making. But if you meet a computer engineer whose engineering
quality is poor (in terms of personality), he may find it difficult to play his
role, and domestic politics may be relaxed as he tries to keep his job or
leans on bluffs and bluster to survive.
As mentioned in the previous chapter, one of Miller Heiman’s most
important clients is the coach. It’s time for an anecdote.
I remember a time when one of my sales teams was very happy after
his return on the 19th with one of his potential candidates who said that he
had found a coach in the business and that the coach was helping us.
However, after successfully passing the personality test, we discovered that
our coach is very likely to move (someone who always starts things, tells
everyone, but rarely finishes something). We quickly concluded that this
person would likely help our competitors and us. We changed our strategy
accordingly, found another coach, and got the job.
The best coach for a politician is someone who wants their way, who
has the authority and who has the motivation to do it. Miller Heiman and
other sales processes do not have this element.
Neuro-linguistic programming (NLP)
Thus, marketing empathy identifies 7 primary emotions and we know
that we have to adjust the way we sell to support the characteristics that
these personality types represent. But that is not enough to build a great
equalizer. NLP, which has its supporters (and which has its skeptics), fills
the gaps, but it is a vast topic and again, there are hundreds of books. When
you start reading them, you may be confused because it is so complete.
As with most things, there are “elements” of NLP that can help
suppliers, and I took NLP as follows:
It will help you better present and communicate by understanding how
people are programmed to receive and count information.
It will help you look at sales situations from the perspective of others.
This will help you focus on people’s faces when you speak to them,
which will make it appear that you are interested in what they are saying.
This will help you gain confidence before an important meeting or
presentation.
The question of whether NLP provides verified data on human
behavior and functioning is very controversial. Sales staff should use what
they are doing, and I will review what I have seen working on the sales
podium.
How people are wired
When we are born, we are programmed to receive information in three
powerful ways, and people will have the preferred means of obtaining
information.
Visual: These people want to see things in pictures, so they will turn
off if there is a lot of text and written material.
Kinesthetic: More delicate people who wish to collect a report or use
their product or service for a demonstration.
Listener: These people learn by listening and are easily distracted by
noise. They like to read, but have trouble writing because they can calculate
better.
These definitions can be adapted to most people. If we try to combine
what the three previous categories tell us, with little empathy sales, we can
see that, for example, movers and artists are normally visual. Engineers and
dual testers are often kinesthetic. Motorcycles, politicians, and double
ladies will be heard.
My point here is that every time you make a presentation, be sure to
communicate in three ways. Never have a performance full of words
because the visuals will not respond. Instead, don’t make presentations that
are just pictures - they will leave hearing and kinesthetic people fresh. Your
submissions should offer something of everything.
During our launch, I made sure to have brochures during the
presentation, especially for kinesthesia. It was exciting to see how these
people use advertisements. They hadn’t read them at the time, but they liked
to “wander” and add substance to the presentation. Do not leave leaflets on
the table to share them at the end, because the kinesthetic will want to catch
them as soon as possible and will be frustrated during the presentation.
In the United States, an excellent example of the use of 5 senses (we
only included 3 of them: sight/seeing, sound/hearing, and touch/kinetics) is
in real estate. Real estate agents know the tricks of the trade. When you
open the tour: you will enter the property. On the move, you will find soft
background music (listening) and a coffee maker with a sweet smell
(smell/smell, it’s a new sense) and you can be invited to try delicious
cookies on the kitchen counter (taste/flavor, last of 5). The agent will ask
people to feel things like doorknobs physically, surfaces (due to their
quality), and clients to look closely at specific features.

It may have been the biggest story since the atom bomb.
The headline, however, was small and ignored the larger
issue. "Drug Tests by CIA Held More Extensive Than Re-
ported in '75," said the New York Times on July 16, 1977.
What it should have said is "U.S. Develops Invisible Weap-
ons to Enslave Mankind."
The testing of drugs by the CIA was just a part of the
United States government's top-secret mind-control proj-
ect, a project which had spanned thirty-five years and had
involved tens of thousands of individuals. It involved tech-
niques of hypnosis, narco-hypnosis, electronic brain stimu-
lation, behavioral effects of ultrasonic, microwave, and
low-frequency sound, aversive and other behavior modifi-
cation therapies. In fact, there was virtually no aspect of
human behavioral control that was not explored in their
search for the means to control the memory and will of
both individuals and whole masses of people.
The CIA succeeded in developing a whole range of
psycho-weapons to expand its already ominous psychologi-
cal warfare arsenal. With these capabilities, it was now pos-
sible to wage a new kind of war—a war which would take
place invisibly, upon the battlefield of the human mind.

boasted Dr. George Estabrooks in the early 1940s.
Estabrooks, chairman of the Department of Psychology
at Colgate University, was called to Washington by the
War Department shortly after Pearl Harbor. Since he was
the ranking authority on hypnosis at the time, they wanted
his opinion on how the enemy might be planning to use
hypnotism. "Two hundred trained foreign operators, work-
ing in the United States," Estabrooks told the military lead-

cally controlled Sixth Columnists."1
At that time, only a handful of men knew of the
government's experiments with hypnosis for the purpose of
controlling minds in the interest of "national security." In
that decade there had been no concentrated assassinations of
presidents, candidates, or civil rights leaders. There had not
yet been Watergate, nor any disclosures of government
agencies invading the privacy of United States citizens. The
CIA had not yet been conceived, and even its parent, the
Office of Strategic Services (OSS), did not exist.

government would employ mind-control techniques on its
own people. Therefore it was natural for George Esta-
brooks to believe that if America were threatened by hyp-

enemy working within the United States.

Preface 9
Preface
In 1992, following the success of my book Crossfire: The
Plot That Killed Kennedy, I began to look for other dark secrets
being hidden away by the federal government. What I found
led me into an incredible journey through time, space, ESP,
UFOs, censorship, and disinformation.
It began with my discovery of a psychic ability termed
remote viewing, or RV. This phenomenon in the past had
been called clairvoyance, prophecy, or soothsaying. Although
recorded by all cultures throughout human history, it was be-
lieved to be simply an occult fantasy until scientific studies
during the 20th century confirmed its existence.
Despite the fact that remote viewing was developed by
various tax-supported government agencies including the
CIA, the Defense Intelligence Agency, and even the U.S. Army,
a majority of Americans still have never heard of this faculty.
9
10 PSI Spies
But remote viewing forever changed the lives of the men
and women employed in its use. This included people only
tangentially connected to the government-funded RV programs.
This book became one of the casualties in the ongoing
conflict between science and ESP, military secrecy and the
public’s right to know, as well as the never-ending intramural
competition between government agencies and power-seeking
individuals.
What you are about to read was suppressed in the sum-
mer of 1995, four months before the existence of government-
sponsored remote viewing was publicly revealed by a CIA
press release.
The story of remote viewing—then one of our government’s
most closely guarded secrets—now has filtered into cer-
tain aware segments of the public, where it continues to
attract growing fascination and interest. Today, several ex-
perienced viewers are bringing this phenomenal tech-
nology to a wider audience. Others have spoken about it
in books, articles, or public speeches. Even some entre-
preneurs now advertise psychic readings reportedly ac-
complished through RV.
To understand this transition from top-secret government
project to minor public fad, I invite the reader to follow my own
experience with remote viewing.
As I traveled across the country on media tours and speak-
ing engagements during 1991 and 1992, at every opportu-
nity, I would ask, “What do you think is the next big secret
government cover-up?”
Preface 11
The response was almost unanimous: I was told that
people were curious about the UFO phenomenon. I realized
that I was, too. Although I had been aware and curious about
UFO stories since I was a young man in the 1950s, I was no
further along than anyone else in learning the truth of the
matter. I determined that I would research and write about
the topic.
As I began to establish, and reestablish, contacts within
the UFO research community, I was made aware of a speech
presented by a military intelligence officer at a public con-
ference in Atlanta in early 1992 (the Treat IV Conference). In
a public speech, then-Army Captain Ed Dames spoke about
UFOs, detailing in no uncertain terms what they were, where
they came from, and where they were going.
His matter-of-fact tone intrigued me, for here was no
starry-eyed New Age fanatic, but a decorated military intel-
ligence officer. Furthermore, Dames was no loose cannon.
During his talk, he was flanked by Col. John Alexander, a
leading luminary in military nonlethal weapons research
who moved freely between both military and intelligence
programs, and Maj. Gen. Albert Stubblebine, former com-
mander of the Army’s Intelligence and Security Command.
Dames told his audience about the development of re-
mote viewing, which he described as “this profound tool.” He
also spoke of flying “transport vehicles” used to “transport a
type of resource, usually from Mars to Earth, sometimes
through time.” He spoke of giant inhabited underground cav-
erns on Earth and hibernating Martians on Mars, even “tran-
scendental” energy beings who could access our very
minds.
12 PSI Spies
Intrigued, I contacted Dames and soon learned the story
of our military remote viewers. Dames said he and fellow
Army officer David Morehouse were in touch with a New York
literary agent. Both officers said the story of RV was too im-
portant to remain a military secret. They were willing to talk.
And I was willing to listen. To me this was a journalist’s
dream come true, for, if RV was fraudulent, it was a shameful
waste of taxpayer money. If it proved true, it could well repre-
sent a leap forward in human evolution. Either way, it was a
story I knew I had to pursue.
An agreement was reached: I would write about RV and
its use by the military, and Dames and Morehouse would
help supply facts, contacts, and information. In June 1993, I
contracted to publish a book through Harmony Books, a sub-
sidiary of Random House.
Beginning with my contact with Dames in the summer of
1992, I spent three years working on the remote viewing
story. During that time, my research showed that the RV phe-
nomenon was a reality that had been recorded through-
out history. I was introduced to other military viewers,
such as Lyn Buchanan and Mel Riley. I met members of the
oversight committees that monitored the RV program, such
as Dr. Paul Tyler and Col. Alexander. I interviewed Dr. Hal
Puthoff and Ingo Swann, who, along with Russell Targ, were
the men most responsible for the development of RV.
The work was arduous, particularly so because I was
dealing with a subject most people wanted no part of—not
to mention that it involved a top-secret government program.
Many sources refused to be interviewed, and others de-
manded anonymity. Hard facts were difficult to come by.
Preface 13
In mid-1995, as the book was nearing publication and
without consulting me, a Harmony editor paid a small sum to
Morehouse to add some personal recollections to the manu-
script. Morehouse had just resigned from the Army under
contentious circumstances and gone to work for the New York
agent.
The inclusion of Morehouse’s experiences upset Dames,
who apparently had come to view the book as his own per-
sonal biography, despite the fact that all concerned had ini-
tially agreed that it would be about remote viewing and the
military unit rather than about any individual.
Dames, who by this time was claiming to be in contact
with alien grays, sent a letter via an attorney to Harmony dis-
avowing the book, even though he had previously signed an
unprecedented release statement based on my completed
manuscript (sans Morehouse’s paragraphs). I found it most
ironic that this obstruction came from the very person who
had initiated the book in the first place, and nothing he had
contributed had been altered or deleted. Some observers
saw a darker purpose behind Dames’s action.
This darker purpose seemed to have been confirmed by
subsequent events. First, the book’s editor was suddenly of-
fered a job outside New York City and left the project. Inter-
estingly, some months after the book was canceled, he returned

strange wailing cry, similar to the howl of a coyote or wolf,
which rose and fell in tone and intensity as if a wailing si-
ren.
I suddenly saw the fear and apprehension that could
be stirred by 12,000 men advancing with fixed bayonets
while uttering this haunting wail. But, how was I to find con-
firmation of this?
Soon, I [would be] attending a conference of the
International Remote Viewers Association. Here was

my opportunity, I thought. But no one would accommo-
date me when I asked several viewers if they would take
a look at the Rebel yell.
On the final day of the conference, I was seated next
to John Kovacs in the hotel bar. It was crowded and noisy
on this evening. There was standing room only. Patrons
were almost shouting to be heard over the loud music and
blaring TVs.
Offhandedly, I mentioned that I had a remote viewing
target but no one would conduct a viewing for me. I asked
if John would do it, and he shrugged and agreed.
For more than two days I had been carrying around a
conference program with my question accompanied by a
coordinate that I made up and attached to my question.
The question I had written down was, “Describe the
sound of the Rebel yell as uttered at the battle of
Gettysburg, July 1863.” The coordinate number I had as-
signed to this question was 4281/2468.
I sat looking around at the crowd while John placed a
stack of hotel notepaper in front of him and began staring
off into space. Quickly, he began to scribble on the small
note sheets, first one and then another. Within five minutes,
he handed me seven note sheets, filled with letters and
crude drawings.
With a sigh, I told him that I could not decipher the
sheets, and I asked him to simply write down a summary.
I handed him a paper bar napkin. He wrote, “Target is
man made…silver, spinning, in constant motion, yet airy
and open w/ site that is larger than it appears, motion is

the 12,000 men of Gen. George Pickett moving with fixed,
silver bayonets moving across the open, airy, and sunny
field in front of Cemetery Ridge, the whole spectacle much
grander than portrayed in sketches and photographs.
My question—and verification of the old veteran’s re-
cording—came next with his words akin to that of a cyclo-
tron. A cyclotron is an apparatus that charges atomic
particles by an alternating electric field while in circular
motion. This is the basis of a siren, such as the hand-
cranked air raid sirens. The old veteran’s wailing cry was
confirmed by remote viewing.
The words gray-dressed soldiers confirmed to me that
Kovacs was right on target. His description of the object of
the session or target—the Rebel yell—as a means “to pro-
pel and land on target” again was dead on. The yell was to
bolster the men’s courage while demoralizing the enemy
to help win success in achieving their objective or target.
I was stunned. Here was a near-perfect remote view-
ing session done under the most distracting circum-
stances and within five minutes.
This then is the wonder of remote viewing. And remem-
ber: The SRI tests showed that RV is not limited by either
time or space, and that we all have within us the ability to
contact planes of existence other than our own.

About
the Author
Jim Marrs is a native of Fort Worth, Texas. He earned a
B.A. in journalism from the University of North Texas and at-
tended graduate school at Texas Tech before pursuing a ca-
reer in journalism. Since 1980, Jim has been a freelance
writer, author, and public relations consultant. He also pub-
lished a rural weekly newspaper, along with a monthly tour-
ism tabloid, a cable television show, and several videos.
An award-winning journalist, Jim is listed both in Who’s
Who in the World and Who’s Who in America, and has won
several writing and photography awards.
He has appeared on major television networks and cable
channels, as well as numerous national and regional radio
and TV shows. Jim is a current member of the Society of
Professional Journalists, Sigma Delta Chi, and the Investigative
Reporters and Editors.
His other books include Alien Agenda, Rule by Secrecy,
The Terror Conspiracy, and Crossfire, which served as a ba-
sis for Oliver Stone’s movie JFK.
